headline: Inflation cools to 4.2% but rate hike still possible, oil slumps nearly 5%, and Google launches Gemini Omni — a rainy end to the week ahead on the Gold Coast.

portfolio.summary: A mixed day across the portfolio. FUEL.AX was the biggest loser as oil prices cratered nearly 5% last night — that pain flowed straight through to today's close. US names were generally steady last night, with TTWO and GOOGL both nudging higher on GTA 6 buzz and Gemini Omni news respectively. MSFT slipped a little. ASX holdings were all quietly positive.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: Oil (WTI crude) dropped nearly 5% last night after OPEC cut its global demand growth forecast for 2026. Lower oil prices = lower profits for energy companies, and this ETF tracks global energy majors — so that pain hits directly.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Up last night as GTA 6 hype builds. Rockstar's CEO confirmed the marketing blitz kicks off this summer and pre-orders are now open, which keeps investor confidence high ahead of what should be a monster release.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Edged higher last night. Google announced Gemini Omni today — a new all-in-one AI model — which keeps Alphabet front and centre in the AI race and supports the bullish narrative around the stock.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Slipped a touch last night. Despite a recent earnings beat, sentiment has been soft — Investor's Business Daily flagged ongoing 'stock blues' as the market questions whether growth can justify the valuation.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Small gain at today's close, ticking up alongside broader positive sentiment in emerging markets.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: Modest gain today. The cooler inflation print gave bank stocks a mild lift — less rate pressure generally helps sentiment, though some economists still think a hike is coming.

markets.summary: US markets were nearly flat last night — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ barely moved. The big story was oil, which absolutely tanked nearly 5% after OPEC slashed its demand forecast. Gold dipped slightly. The Aussie dollar weakened a little against the USD. ASX 200 data wasn't available for today's close.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — markets in a holding pattern.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big drop last night — OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast, meaning the world is expected to need less oil than previously thought. That hammers oil prices and energy stocks.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Small dip, still historically very elevated.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar eased a little. Still relatively strong. A weaker AUD means your US holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) are worth slightly more in AUD terms.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is inflation — it came in at 4.2% for April, which is cooler than before, partly because fuel costs fell. But economists are split: some say the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) will hold rates at its next meeting, others still think a hike is coming. Bond markets (where big investors bet on interest rate moves) are now pricing in fewer rate rises than before.

stories.title: Inflation eases to 4.2% in April — but rate rise still possible, economists warn
stories.why_it_matters: April CPI (the official measure of how much prices are rising) came in at 4.2% — lower than recent months, helped by falling fuel costs. This is good news, but economists caution it's probably temporary. The Conversation notes that while the RBA is likely to hold rates at its June meeting, underlying inflation is still too high for comfort, and a hike later in the year hasn't been ruled out. The AFR reports bond markets have dialled back their bets on rate rises following the data, which is why bank and property stocks got a mild boost today.

stories.title: Bond markets dial back rate rise bets after inflation cools
stories.why_it_matters: Following the cooler inflation print, the big institutional investors who trade government bonds are now betting that the RBA won't need to raise rates as aggressively as feared. This matters to you because lower expected rates are generally good for growth stocks and property, and tend to support the broader share market.

stories.title: Rate hikes loom despite slowing inflation
stories.why_it_matters: Not everyone is convinced the coast is clear. Some economists warn that the fall in inflation is partly driven by temporary factors like cheaper petrol, and that when those drop out of the data, underlying price pressures will reassert themselves. The RBA may still need to hike rates later in 2026 to get inflation back to its 2-3% target band, which would be bad news for mortgage holders and could weigh on consumer spending.

ai.summary: Two big AI stories today: Google launched Gemini Omni, a new all-in-one AI model, and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 has apparently beaten rivals in a tough coding test. Meanwhile, the new Pope Leo XIV is calling loudly for AI regulation — especially around weapons — and Aussie startup founders are pushing back, wanting a light-touch approach similar to the US.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — its most capable all-in-one AI model yet
stories.why_it_matters: Google today announced Gemini Omni — described as a single unified AI model that can handle text, images, audio, video, and code all at once (what's called a 'multimodal' model, meaning it works across multiple types of content rather than just text). This is Google's answer to OpenAI's GPT-4o and directly relevant to your GOOGL holding. Stronger AI products help Google defend its position in search and cloud computing, both key revenue drivers.

stories.title: GPT-5.5 beats Claude and Gemini in tough new coding benchmark
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI's new GPT-5.5 has topped a 'long-horizon coding benchmark' — basically a test where AI has to write complex software over an extended period, not just answer short questions. It beat both Anthropic's Claude and Google's Gemini on this test. For investors in GOOGL, it's a reminder that the AI race is fierce and Google needs to keep pushing — which is why today's Gemini Omni launch matters.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for strict regulation of AI weapons
stories.why_it_matters: Newly elected Pope Leo XIV — the first American pope — has used an official Vatican document (called an encyclical, basically a formal letter to the global Catholic community) to call for international regulation of AI used in warfare, including autonomous weapons that can select and kill targets without human oversight. The Vatican is urging global governments to act. While this doesn't move markets directly, it adds to the chorus of voices pushing for AI governance laws, which could eventually affect how AI companies like Google and Microsoft develop and sell defence-related products.

stories.title: Aussie founders push for US-style light-touch AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: A group of Australian startup founders is lobbying the federal government to keep AI regulation minimal — similar to the hands-off approach taken in the US — rather than following the EU's stricter rulebook. Their argument is that heavy regulation will stifle innovation and push AI investment offshore. The debate matters for where Australia sits in the global AI ecosystem, and for ASX-listed tech companies that may be affected by whatever framework the government lands on.

sport.summary: The big NRL story is State of Origin Game 1 — NSW pulled off an extraordinary comeback, winning despite having a player sent off. Round 13 team lists are out and there are some notable ins and outs. In AFL, Essendon's coaching saga continues with James Hird putting his hand up. French Open is underway with McEnroe calling for rule changes.

stories.title: 'Greatest escape Origin has ever seen' — NSW win Game 1 despite send-off drama
stories.why_it_matters: NSW Blues produced one of the most stunning Origin wins in history in Game 1, coming back to defeat Queensland despite having a player sent off mid-match — playing most of the game with 12 men. Fox Sports is calling it the 'greatest escape Origin has ever seen.' The result gives the Blues the first-game edge in the series. Full details on the final score weren't in the article text, but the comeback nature of the win has already become the talk of the football world.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 teams: Payne Haas back for Broncos, Nicho Hynes ruled out for Sharks
stories.why_it_matters: Key team news for Round 13: Payne Haas returns for the Broncos (big boost for Brisbane ahead of their Sunday home game against the Dragons at Suncorp). Nicho Hynes has been ruled out for the Sharks, which is a significant blow with their Friday night clash against the Sea Eagles. Several Origin stars are confirmed to back up for their clubs this weekend despite the mid-week representative game.

stories.title: James Hird says he's the right man to make Essendon great again
stories.why_it_matters: Former Essendon captain and coach James Hird has publicly declared he wants to return to the club in a coaching capacity and is putting himself forward as the man to restore the Bombers to their former glory. This comes as the club looks to replace Brad Scott. Hird's return would be one of the most polarising stories in recent AFL history given his involvement in the supplements saga — so expect this to dominate footy talk for a while.

stories.title: 'Tennis is going to die': Champion's dire warning at French Open
stories.why_it_matters: A prominent tennis figure — the article doesn't name them in the available text — has issued a stark warning at Roland Garros (the French Open) that the sport faces an existential crisis if current trends continue. Separately, John McEnroe has used his French Open commentary role to call for a major rule change. The French Open is the marquee clay-court Grand Slam and currently underway in Paris.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — oil price slump is a real headwind
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil dropped nearly 5% last night after OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast. That's the direct reason FUEL.AX fell 1.82% today. If oil stays under pressure, this ETF will keep drifting lower. No need to panic-sell, but worth watching whether the oil weakness continues — if it does, revisit your position sizing.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 marketing blitz confirmed for this summer
watch_today.detail: Rockstar's CEO has confirmed the GTA 6 marketing campaign kicks off this (northern hemisphere) summer, with pre-orders now open. This is a significant positive catalyst — GTA 6 is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches ever. The stock is up on the news. Hold and watch how the campaign builds momentum into the release.

watch_today.title: GOOGL — Gemini Omni launch keeps Google in the AI race
watch_today.detail: Google launched Gemini Omni today — a unified multimodal AI model (one model handling text, images, audio, video and code). It's a direct response to OpenAI's GPT-4o. The stock nudged up last night. The AI investment thesis for Alphabet remains intact. Hold comfortably.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision watch — inflation data shifts the odds
watch_today.detail: Today's 4.2% CPI (inflation) print has reduced the chance of a near-term RBA rate hike, with bond markets dialling back their rate rise bets. This is broadly good for your ASX holdings — lower rates support both growth stocks and banks like CBA. However, economists warn the cool inflation may be temporary (fuel prices won't stay low forever), so a hike later in 2026 is still possible. Keep an eye on next month's data.

watch_today.title: MSFT — sentiment still soft despite earnings beat
watch_today.detail: Microsoft slipped again last night and Investor's Business Daily is asking whether it's a sell after the stock has failed to rally following a strong earnings result. The market seems to be questioning whether AI investments will deliver returns fast enough. Nothing has fundamentally broken — hold for now, but it's worth watching whether the weakness continues into next week.
